draft.title: Sequence and structure of an argument
card: A persuasive piece is built in a planned order. The order of the parts shapes how a reader meets the ideas and what they take away.
often an anecdote, a question or a striking fact. It grabs attention and sets up the issue, and the writer's view may appear here or soon after.
a run of paragraphs, each building one argument. A writer may put a strong point first to win the reader, or save it for last to finish with force.
often a call to action, which asks readers to do something, or a closing point that restates the writer's view. When you analyse structure, ask why each part sits where it does.
draft.remember: Order is a choice: each part's place is meant to guide the reader towards the writer's view.

a.q: An opinion piece opens with a short story about a teenager who cannot get a bus home at night. What is the main purpose of this opening?
opts: To draw the reader in and introduce the issue
To give the final statistics that prove the case
To ask the reader to take a particular action
To answer the arguments of the opposing side
a.why: An opening anecdote grabs attention and sets up the issue through a human case. A call to action usually comes near the end, so asking for action is the tempting but wrong choice here.
a.clue: Think about what a writer needs to do in the first few lines.

b.q: Priya writes an article on school start times. Her last paragraph tells readers to email their local MP this week. How does this ending work on the reader?
opts: It turns the reader's agreement into a step to take
It gives the reader a fresh argument to weigh up
It introduces the issue so the reader can follow
It lets the reader see the opposing side's views
b.why: A call to action at the end moves readers from agreeing to acting, so it works as a final push. It does not add a new argument. Introducing the issue is the job of the opening, not the ending.
b.clue: Emailing an MP is something the reader is asked to do.

a.best: To draw the reader in and introduce the issue

b.best: It turns the reader's agreement into a step to take
